{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOI30vQc8AAAABbForIg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm3E6zhEqwSc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm3E6", "number": 26, "title": "Document three concise UI/UX and layout principles", "body": "## Problem

The maintained documentation does not currently provide a concise UI/UX and layout baseline comparable to the [three UI/UX principles in my-audio-to-text](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#uiux). A short shared baseline will help contributors and AI agents avoid unnecessary information, controls, explanations, and unexpected interactions.

## Expected outcome

Add a short UI/UX section to the existing `README.md`, preferably beside existing design principles where present, with exactly these three principles:

1. **Keep it simple.** Show only necessary information and actions; avoid unnecessary UI elements.
2. **Show, don't tell.** Prefer layout, spacing and visual hierarchy over explanatory labels or prose to communicate structure.
3. **Intuitive and predictable.** Keep appearance and behavior consistent with user expectations; don't interrupt the user's work.

“Show, don't tell” must not remove necessary control labels, accessible names, error messages, or information needed to use the interface. Simplification must preserve meaningful consent, destructive-action safeguards, and necessary warnings.

Add a brief link to that section from the existing `docs/review-guidelines.md` so applicable interface changes are reviewed against it. Keep one canonical statement of the three principles instead of duplicating them or adding another checklist.

Apply the principles to the repository's actual user-facing surfaces. For a CLI- or library-focused repository, document their applicability to existing commands, messages, examples, and any future graphical interface; this task does not introduce a GUI or new product surface. Preserve existing architecture, behavior, and project-specific documentation.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The existing README states the three concise principles above and is easy to find.
- [ ] Existing review guidance links to the canonical section without repeating lengthy rules.
- [ ] Essential labels, accessibility information, errors, and necessary user decisions remain explicitly supported.
- [ ] Existing relevant guidance is preserved; the change is documentation only, with no new policy document, design system, UI implementation, dependency, or unrelated refactor.
- [ ] Check Markdown structure, relative links and heading anchors, consistency, and whitespace using available tooling. New runtime tests, application builds, physical-device checks, deployed-site checks, or human design approval are not required for this documentation-only change.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

Requested across repositories managed by ProjectWeave that do not already document UI/UX or layout principles. Follow this repository's existing Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge flow and collaboration-language conventions.
